title: Tech Note: 4D v11 SQL Pass-Through without ODBC
author: Charles Vass, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.

historical_commentary.text: This technical note documents a major advancement in 4D v11 SQL Release 3: the introduction of native, direct SQL pass-through communications between 4D Server and 4D Professional applications via TCP/IP, eliminating the need for ODBC drivers or intervening layers. This feature addressed a long-standing gap left by the discontinuation of the 4D Open plug-in (which had facilitated database-to-database communication in pre-SQL versions). The note covers the conceptual rationale, detailed SQL LOGIN/LOGOUT syntax, field-level change tracking with ownership and collision prevention, and the new picture variable/array BLOB storage capability introduced in Release 3. While modern 4D has evolved significantly beyond SQL pass-through to embrace ORDA, REST APIs, and remote object methods, the core concepts of synchronous data exchange and secure inter-process communication remain foundational.
related_updates: ORDA (Object-Relational Data Model, 4D v2018+) provides a modern, object-centric alternative to SQL pass-through for inter-application communication and data synchronization
4D Remote Objects and modern REST/WebSocket APIs have largely replaced direct SQL pass-through as the preferred mechanism for database-to-application communication

SSL encryption for SQL connections evolved into modern TLS/certificate-based security in current 4D versions; the concept of SQL connection security remains valid but implementation details have advanced
